title: A Time for Everything
backstory: The Preacher has already learned that money never fills the hole it promises to fill — he that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver (Ecclesiastes 5:10). So he turns and looks at time instead: to every thing there is a season, a time to plant and a time to pluck up, a time to weep and a time to laugh, and God makes every one of them beautiful in his time (Ecclesiastes 3:1-11). Then he notices one more thing — two are better than one, for if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow (Ecclesiastes 4:9-10). This life was never meant to be walked alone.

passages.synopsis: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven. There is a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to reap. There is a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance. Every season of life has its place in God's design.

The Preacher sees that God hath made every thing beautiful in his time. God has also set the world in man's heart — a longing for things that last for ever. To eat, to drink, and to enjoy the good of our labour is the gift of God. Whatever God does shall stand for ever, so that men should fear before him.

Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labour. If one falls, his friend can lift him up, but woe to him that is alone when he falleth. Two lying together keep warm, and two can stand against an enemy that would overcome one. A threefold cord is not quickly broken.

triviaQuestions.question: What does Ecclesiastes say there is for every purpose under the heaven?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:1 — "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:"

triviaQuestions.question: What does the Preacher say God has set in man's heart?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:11 — "He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end."

triviaQuestions.question: Why are two better than one?
options: They have a good reward for their labour
triviaQuestions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:9 — "Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour."

triviaQuestions.question: What is not quickly broken?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:12 — "And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken."

scrambleVerses.text: To every thing there is a season
a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

reflection: God has set a time for every season of life and makes everything beautiful in his time. Can you trust his timing in the season you are in right now?
